comment: The four entry points are a useful diagnostic, but small states often fall under entry points 1 and 2 at the same time: limited national governance and foundational DPI, alongside several donor-funded, programme-specific systems already in operation. The text presents the entry points as alternatives and does not explain how to sequence the work when more than one applies.

anchor.note: p.89–90 l.63–101 read as the printed page; section 4.2.1 agrees

public.text: The four entry points are a useful diagnostic, but small states often fall under entry points 1 and 2 at the same time: limited national governance and foundational DPI, alongside several donor-funded, programme-specific systems already in operation. The text presents the entry points as alternatives and does not explain how to sequence the work when more than one applies.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a sentence noting that a country can fall under more than one entry point at the same time. Explain how to sequence the work in that case; for example, establishing architectural standards and governance under entry point 1 before starting the integration work described under entry point 2.
